text:
alyssa: Observed a slow memory growth/regression on Qwen-MQA during long-context sessions when rope scaling > 64k. Noticed incremental page counts even after evictions kick in.
ben: Is this the thing that started after the kernel-selection change last week?
alyssa: Looks correlated. Deploy at 1964010000 touched kernel heuristics + slab allocator tweak. Perf traces attached.
carlos: Pushed a quick pprof sample from a repro run:```
# pprof -pdf kv_cache cpu
Time: 2026-03-17T14:12:03Z
Sample: 30s of process
Top functions:
  kv::alloc_page     38.2%  (hot)
  kv::evict_candidate 22.5%
  runtime::sweep     12.1%
  kernel::gqa_dispatch 9.3%
Metrics:
  pages_allocated: 4823 -> 14923 (10m)
  page_frag_ratio: 0.64 -> 0.78
```
maria: That frag ratio is brutal. Is it MQA-specific?
alyssa: Mostly MQA and Qwen variants. Llama/Mistral not hitting the same pattern; they reuse pages better.
ben: Hypothesis: MQA slot sizes interact badly with our slab sizes and rope-scaled kv entries, causing small tail allocations that never coalesce.
carlos: Repro script (local):```bash
# repro-long-kv.sh
./run_infer --model qwen-mqa --context 120000 --seq-sweep 1 --alloc-slab=64k --trace-kv > kv.log
```
alyssa: Repro on a dedicated host shows steady mem climb ~200MB / 10min until OOM if left. Evictions trigger but keep allocating new pages.
maria: Could be our eviction policy prefers LRU across full pages, but MQA per-token keys cause high churn inside pages. Evicting whole pages loses reuse potential.
ben: Quick mitigation idea: enable per-model page pools and compact-on-attach for MQA models. That should reduce cross-model fragmentation.
carlos: Another temp fix: lower slab size to 16k for MQA builds and bump compaction frequency. I tested that locally: peak pages dropped ~30%.
alyssa: We should also verify kernel selection: the new GQA-optimized kernel uses wider KV layout which might increase internal fragmentation for MQA. If kernel chooses GQA layout for MQA by mistake, that'll blow up memory.
ben: Good catch. Add a guard to kernel selector: prefer explicit MQA layout for models flagged MQA in metadata.
maria: Also think about batching heuristics: huge batches increase simultaneous KV attachments and amplify fragmentation. For long-context streams, favor smaller batches with dynamic batching threshold.
carlos: Filed a quick PR reverting just the allocator tweak: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/4216 (draft). Repro seems much better on that branch.
alyssa: +1 to canary that PR in a low-traffic region. If we see mem slope flatten, we can roll forward or iterate.
ben: Add perf test to nightly: long-context Qwen-MQA 120k, measure pages_allocated and page_frag_ratio at 5/30/60m.
maria: I'll add test. Also add tracepoint for "page_owner" to see which model/thread creates the fragment.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for cluster-us-east-2 (PR 4216). ETA 20m.
alyssa: For follow-ups: 1) canary PR 4216 2) add per-model pool experiment 3) kernel selector guard 4) batching heuristic tweak 5) add perf tests + alert on frag_ratio>0.6.
carlos: I'll own 1 & 3. ben: I'll prototype per-model pool. maria: I'll add perf test and add tracepoints.
alyssa: Cool. If anyone finds quick workaround flags we can enable remotely, post here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
